transitions.label: 4d5.(6S).5p z 7P°4 - 4d5.(6S).6d g 7D5, 415.907 nm
transitions.use: second step of a two-colour, three-photon resonance-ionization scheme of Mo: 379.933 nm (a7S3 - z7P4), then 415.907 nm (z7P4 - 4d5 6d 7D5), then ionization by either colour; demonstrated with optogalvanic detection in a hollow-cathode lamp

use_source.value: measured peak wavelengths 379.93341(4) nm and 415.90717(10) nm (pulsed dye lasers, wavemeter; Lorentzian fits)
use_source.source: Lu, Varvarezos, Nicolosi, Andrighetto, Scarpa, Mariotti, Costello, Phys. Scr. 97, 024004 (2022), Sections 2-3 and Fig. 3 (open access)

transitions.note: the 6d 7D5 level is identified with NIST g 7D5 at 50364.243 cm^-1 (26320.42 + 10^7/415.907 = 50364.2); no rate measured

conflicts: A(z7P4 -> a5D4, 715 nm): Paladugu et al. 2025 measure 1.15(20)e3 s^-1 from MOT loss; NIST ASD / Whaling & Brault 1988 give 6(2)e5 s^-1 (500 times larger; Whaling & Brault themselves flag self-absorption problems for the z7P branching fractions) and Palmeri & Wyart theory 4e4 s^-1. The MOT value is kept.

Isotope shifts of the 379.8 nm line: Paladugu et al. 2025 vs Aufmuth et al. 1978 differ by more than 2 sigma for 92-96 (920.4(1.9) vs 899(3) MHz) and 100-96 (-812.0(1.9) vs -803(1) MHz); Aufmuth uncertainties are statistical only. Paladugu values kept.

z7P lifetimes: Kwiatkowski et al. 1981 (16.3(8), 15.8(8), 14.7(7) ns for J = 2, 3, 4) vs Duquette et al. 1981 (17.1, 17.0, 15.9 ns, +-5 %) vs Whaling et al. 1984 (z7P4: 14.5(4) ns, derived from the quoted decay rate). All agree within about 1.5 sigma; Kwiatkowski kept as entry because it was read directly.
Isotopic abundances: IAEA Live Chart values are used; the NIST Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions page lists slightly different numbers (e.g. 95Mo 15.84(11) %, 98Mo 24.39(37) %).
z7D3 (31654.786) lifetime: Kwiatkowski et al. 1981 (kept), Jiang et al. 2013 21.4(10) ns and Whaling et al. 1984 21.5(5) ns (as quoted by Jiang) all agree within errors.
x5D3 (40488.28) lifetime: Jiang et al. 2013 15.9(10) ns (entry, read directly) vs Whaling et al. 1984 15.0(10) ns (second-hand); agree within errors.

z7D3 branching fractions: Jiang et al. 2013 vs the 'Previous' column they quote from Whaling et al.: a5S2 0.0025(1) vs 0.006, a5D2 0.0005(1) vs 0.0012, a5D4 0.0030(1) vs 0.00009 (a factor of about 30 for the last one). Jiang values are entered; where the NIST line list carries the older A value the two will differ accordingly.
not_found: Lifetimes of the drawn odd levels still without a value (z5F, z5D, y5D, x5D other than x5D3, y5F, w5D, u5F, t5F, 3D/3F levels ...): measured for 56 levels by Whaling, Hannaford, Lowe, Biemont, Grevesse, J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transfer 32, 69 (1984) (doi:10.1016/0022-4073(84)90007-4), still closed. Only the two Whaling values that Jiang et al. 2013 quote (z7D3 21.5(5) ns, x5D3 15.0(10) ns) could be entered, as 'compilation' alternatives. Hannaford & Lowe, Opt. Eng. 22(5) (1983) likewise not accessible.

Hyperfine constants A, B of 95Mo/97Mo in the metastable a5S2, a5D0-4 levels and in z7P2,3,4 and other odd levels: measured by Olsson et al., Phys. Scr. 29, 61 (1984) and 34, 24 (1986), Brenner et al., Z. Phys. A 316, 247 (1984) and Pendlebury & Ring, J. Phys. B 5 (doi:10.1088/0022-3700/5/2/035); the abstracts opened give no numbers and the full texts (IOP, Springer) were not accessible.

Isotope shifts in Mo I lines other than 379.8 nm (Aufmuth et al. 1978, 16 lines; Goble & Palmer, J. Phys. B 18, 2181 (1985); Olsson et al. 1986): full texts not accessible. The abstract of Aufmuth et al. gives only relative delta<r^2> values.
Measured Lande g factors beyond those already in the NIST levels file (Brenner et al. 1984 measured gJ of a5D, a5S, a5P, c5D by atomic-beam magnetic resonance): values not accessible.
Resonance-ionization schemes for Mo: one open scheme is now entered (Lu et al. 2022, 379.933 nm + 415.907 nm, see transitions); the CERN RILIS database requires a login and was not used.

Measured branching fractions newer than Whaling & Brault 1988 (the NIST source) other than the two z7P4 leak rates above: none located. The full Whaling & Brault table is hosted at http://kurucz.harvard.edu/atoms/4200/whalingbrault.dat and is what NIST ASD already carries.

Routes tried for Whaling et al. 1984 (three passes): OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar ('closed', no repository location), Crossref, OSTI ETDEWEB, arXiv API, CORE, CaltechAUTHORS record search (no entry for this paper), ORBi (Liege) search, Wayback Machine (only a 403 capture of the ScienceDirect page), Kurucz atoms/4200 (whalingbrault.dat and ewhalingbrault.dat hold the Whaling & Brault 1988 branching fractions and level energies but no lifetimes; life4200.dat is calculated and was not entered), the NASA ADS scan of Biemont, Grevesse, Hannaford, Lowe, Whaling, Astrophys. J. 275, 889 (1983) (3 pages, solar abundance from 12 lines, no lifetime table), and the open review Veklich et al., J. Astrophys. Astron. 36, 589 (2015) (g*f values of 7 lines only). Jiang et al., J. Opt. Soc. Am. B 30, 489 (2013) WAS obtained in this pass: the tables embedded in the publisher abstract page were read from a Wayback Machine copy (saved as pdf/Mo_Jiang_2013.html).

Hyperfine constants of the metastable a5S2 and a5D levels: Brenner, Buettgenbach, Glaeser, Kloster, Roeder, Rupprecht, Traeber, Z. Phys. A 316, 247 (1984) (abstract read on OSTI and via Wayback: A, B and g_J measured for a5D, a5S, a5P, c5D by ABMR, plus isotope shifts) and Dubke, Jitschin, Meisel, Childs, Phys. Lett. A 65, 109 (1978) (abstract: B factors of metastable levels, giving Q(95Mo) = -0.015(4) b, Q(97Mo) = +0.017(4) b, Q97/Q95 = -11.50(3)) print no level constants in their abstracts

Third pass, hyperfine structure and isotope shifts: Olsson et al., Phys. Scr. 29, 61 (1984) and 34, 24 (1986) and the 1985 J. Phys. B 18 paper (doi:10.1088/0022-3700/18/11/012; the latter two flagged 'bronze' open by OpenAlex) are served only behind the IOP captcha page, and the Wayback Machine holds only abstract pages or redirects; Brenner et al., Z. Phys. A 316, 247 (1984) (Springer, closed; Wayback has the abstract page only). The published version of the Mo MOT paper (Phys. Rev. A 112, 063112 (2025), NIST copy) mentions the 95Mo/97Mo hyperfine structure but gives no constants.

Fourth pass (2026-10-02), publisher pages addressed directly with the WebFetch tool: no new numbers. IOP (Goble & Palmer, J. Phys. B 18, 2181 (1985), doi:10.1088/0022-3700/18/11/012; Olsson, Olsson, Robertsson, Rosen, Phys. Scr. 38, 707 (1988), doi:10.1088/0031-8949/38/5/010): both /article/<doi> and /article/<doi>/pdf redirect to the bot-check page (validate.perfdrive.com), not followed. The Wayback captures of the Phys. Scr. 29 and 38 pages (2025-08-09, 2026-07-02) are the abstract page with 'The computer you are using is not registered by an institution with a subscription', i.e. these two are paywalled, not open; the Olsson 1984 abstract gives only Q(97Mo)/Q(95Mo) = -11.48(1), no A or B constants. Elsevier (Whaling et al. 1984, pii 0022407384900074): HTTP 403 on sciencedirect.com (both /pii/ and /abs/pii/), linkinghub shows only a redirect stub. Springer (Aufmuth et al., Z. Phys. A 285, 357, doi:10.1007/BF01813235; Brenner et al., Z. Phys. A 316, 247, doi:10.1007/BF01412273): PDF and article addresses loop through the idp.springer.com cookie redirect and return no text. APS (Siegel, Lawler, Couillaud, Haensch, Phys. Rev. A 23, 2457 (1981), isotope shifts of nine a5D - z5P lines to 2 MHz): PDF address HTTP 401, abstract page only, no numbers. SPIE (Hannaford & Lowe, Opt. Eng. 22, 532 (1983), doi:10.1117/12.7973193): empty page. OSTI ETDEWEB records 5321344 (Olsson 1986), 5297775 (Goble & Palmer) and 5755654: abstracts only, no full-text link. Also checked without result: CaltechAUTHORS record API (no Mo I paper by Whaling), the Kurucz atoms/4200 laboratory files gf4200wh.lab / wb7 / sd / cb (log gf of a few lines, no lifetimes, not entered), the Semantic Scholar list of 33 papers citing Whaling et al. 1984 (the open ones are plasma-diagnostic and abundance papers without a lifetime table), and the full text of arXiv:2507.12291v4 (re-read as PDF: only the Table II isotope shifts already stored; it refers to Olsson et al. for the a5D4 - z7P4 shifts without printing them). OpenAlex was out of its shared daily budget.
notes: Lifetimes from Kwiatkowski 1981 and Duquette 1981 were read from the abstracts of the original papers (the abstracts list the numbers); the papers themselves are paywalled. Hyperfine constants of the ground state are the directly measured (uncorrected) ABMR values in MHz, B converted from kHz. Isotope shifts are nu(first) - nu(second). Frequencies are for 98Mo (boson, no hyperfine structure). The 15 lifetime entries above 39000 cm^-1 are J >= 5 levels that the site does not draw yet; the Whaling-Chevako-Lawler numbers were read from an OCR text layer of the scanned paper and checked by eye for the obvious OCR slips (e.g. "t4.0" = 14.0). Second pass: no new numerical entries could be sourced for Mo; see not_found for what was tried. Third pass: 13 new level lifetimes (44951.5-47184.5 cm^-1; none of these levels is drawn by the site at present, but they are the only TR-LIF lifetimes openly readable), one more lifetime for x5D3 (40488.28), and 129 transition rates with branching fractions were taken from Jiang et al. 2013 (Tables 2 and 3). Table 3 prints g_k*A_ki in units of 10^7 s^-1; A_s here is that number divided by g_k = 2J_upper+1 and is marked 'derived' in the note; its uncertainty is the printed one divided by g_k. Check done: lifetime x sum(A) = 0.995-1.000 for all 13 upper levels (the paper normalises the branching fractions to 1). Level energies in Jiang's tables are rounded to 0.01 cm^-1 and were matched to the NIST levels by energy and J.
